course_name_original: Análisis y Diseño de Sistemas de Fluidos
course_name_en: Analysis and Design of Fluid Systems
prerequisites: Prior acquisition of competencies and learning outcomes from more basic subjects covering fluid motion (liquids and gases) and associated energy transfer processes, including operating principles of incompressible fluid machinery. These competencies should have been acquired in the bachelor's degree (e.g., Industrial Technologies Engineering or other industrial engineering degrees).

learning_outcomes.text: Analyze, design, and project fluid installations in the fields of industry, building, public works, energy generation, and transport.
Carry out projects for noise assessment and control and acoustic conditioning in the fields of industry, building, public works, energy generation, and transport.
Understand and apply legislation, regulations, and technical codes related to fluid installations and acoustic conditioning projects.
Evaluate and minimize environmental and social impacts of actions and projects related to fluid installations.
Communicate correctly to any type of audience, both in written and oral form, the results of actions and projects of fluid installations and acoustic conditioning.

syllabus_topics: Pneumatic transport of particles and separation.
Hydraulic and wind energy utilization systems.

assessment_methods.method: Practical work (T1): individual work on sizing and selection of a pressure group for building water supply
Practical work (T2): pair work on optimal operation of a pumping system with parallel pumps and variable speed
Practical work (T3): individual work on design and sizing for minimum consumption of a pneumatic transport system
Practical work (T4): pair work on design, modeling, and calculation of a sprinkler fire fighting system
Practical work (T5): pair work on CFD modeling, calculation, and analysis of indoor ventilation
Final exam (E): questions and numerical exercises on all course contents

assessment_rules: The final grade (NF) for the ordinary examination is calculated as: NF=0.05·T1 + 0.1·T2 + 0.1·T3 + 0.05·T4 + 0.1·T5 + 0.6·E, where grades for each practical work and the final exam are out of 10 points. No minimum grade is required for individual practical works or the final exam. For students with differentiated evaluation, the final grade will be that of the final exam E. In the extraordinary examination, scores from all practical works (T1 to T5) completed during the course will be retained, and the same criteria and considerations as in the ordinary examination will apply.
